context.objective: Document how we carry out European Bank Account Administration, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: To begin with, we confirm request, entity, and regional route. Before starting we need approved request and entity information. What we do: confirm whether the event is a new account, bank transition, mandate change, or signatory refresh; confirm legal entity and jurisdiction; identify the applicable regional review chain; record the business need and target timing. The check on it: confirm the correct entity and jurisdiction before submission. Next, we assemble the bank documentation package. Before starting we need expected activity, investor profile, economic purpose, and regulatory information. What we do: prepare the expected activity profile; prepare the investor profile using approved KYC and AML sources; document the economic purpose; include applicable regulatory thresholds and supporting records; complete bank-specific forms without changing approved facts. The check on it: confirm that all information can be traced to approved sources.
Talk me through what happens after the bank documentation package is assembled.

After that, we confirm CDD, mandate, and signatory readiness. Before starting we need CDD status and information about authorized signatories. What we do: confirm the required KYC and CDD status through and the current regional schedule; prepare the bank mandate and signatory information; for a transition, refresh the mandate and signatories instead of reusing them without review; apply the callback-verification checks to new or changed payment instructions when applicable. The check on it: do not use unsupported or outdated signatory information. Then, we complete regional review and submit to bank. Before starting we need complete package and approved mandate. What we do: route the package through the applicable Administration, Fund Accounting, Controller, and Head of Jurisdiction review chain; resolve review comments; submit through the bank-approved channel; keep the submission record. The check on it: obtain the required regional approval before submission.
What confirms the account administration is complete after submission to the bank?

Once that is done, we resolve bank queries and regulatory exceptions. Before starting we need bank query or identified regulatory issue. What we do: record the query and prepare the response from approved records; obtain regional or client approval for changed facts or additional written confirmations; if a Guernsey financial-resources or liquidity breach is identified, escalate it so the GFSC receives immediate written notice; keep the response and decision record. The check on it: do not provide a speculative response or delay a required GFSC notification. Following that, we confirm account, mandate, and Kyriba setup. Before starting we need bank confirmation of the account opening or transition. What we do: confirm the account identity and status from bank records; confirm mandate and signatories match the approved package; confirm that Treasury can see the account in Kyriba when it is in scope; update approved operational records. Do not store unredacted bank data outside authorized locations. The check on it: confirm that the bank setup matches the approved mandate and signatories.
After you confirm the account, mandate, and Kyriba setup, what observable condition tells you the administration work is finished?

notes.summary: After submission, the team handles bank queries and regulatory issues using approved records, obtains approval for changed facts or additional confirmations, and escalates specified Guernsey breaches for immediate GFSC notice. For openings and transitions it checks bank-confirmed setup, mandate and signatories, Kyriba visibility when applicable, and operational records. Overall closure and accountability remain open.

For an account opening or transition, the participant describes bank confirmation, checks of account status and approved mandate and signatories, Treasury visibility in Kyriba when in scope, and updated operational records.

Before submission, the bank documentation package is assembled: an expected activity profile and economic purpose are prepared, an investor profile is prepared using approved KYC and AML sources, applicable regulatory thresholds and supporting records are included, and bank-specific forms are completed without changing approved facts.
After assembling the package, the team confirms CDD, mandate and signatory readiness using CDD status and authorized-signatory information. It confirms required KYC and CDD status and the current regional schedule, and prepares the bank mandate and signatory information. For a transition it refreshes the mandate and signatories rather than reusing them without review; callback-verification checks apply to new or changed payment instructions when applicable.
The source or method used to confirm KYC and CDD status needs clarification; the participant's description is incomplete at that point.
With a complete package and approved mandate, the team routes the package through the applicable Administration, Fund Accounting, Controller and Head of Jurisdiction review chain, resolves review comments, submits through the bank-approved channel and keeps the submission record. Required regional approval precedes submission.
When a bank query or regulatory issue arises, the team records it and prepares a response from approved records. It obtains regional or client approval for changed facts or additional written confirmations, and keeps the response and decision record.
If a Guernsey financial-resources or liquidity breach is identified, the team escalates it so the GFSC receives immediate written notice.
After bank confirmation of an account opening or transition, the team confirms account identity and status against bank records, matches the mandate and signatories to the approved package, checks Treasury can see the account in Kyriba when in scope, and updates approved operational records.
